title: Packaging Mockup Generator for Product Scenes | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a square shelf, counter, or cafe preview from one photo of the pouch, box, or bottle you will ship. This picture is not the printed pack.
h1: Packaging Mockup Generator for a Shelf or Cafe Scene
lead: A paper coffee pouch can open the ad before anyone writes a prompt. Set the bag in the frame. The spoken line names the roast you actually ship.

steps.d: Use the product-page photo with the pouch front facing you. A paper coffee pouch on the cafe counter fits this layout.
Say what the pouch should tell buyers, such as a morning roast. An avatar you choose for this shop speaks the line.
Save the square preview of the pouch for the shop grid. A tall file can go to the person who runs the ads.

steps_h2: Make a Shelf Preview From One Package Photo in 3 Steps
steps_lead: A photo of the coffee pouch starts it. You leave holding a square preview the shop can post.

faq.q: What is a packaging video ad template?
faq.a: A packaging template is a shopper frame that already knows the shelf, waiting for the pack you sell. Set a photo of the paper coffee pouch in that frame and the clip can show the front panel. Nobody has to book a studio for this version.

faq.q: How does a packaging template turn into a finished ad?
faq.a: You finish with a file the shop can publish. The pouch's product page supplies the front panel. You rewrite one sentence so it names the roast. The square file is what you drop into the ad account.

faq.q: Why use a template instead of hiring someone to film?
faq.a: A hired creator puts the next cut on their calendar. When the coffee pouch's weekend price changes, you rewrite the offer in this file. You can post the new cut while the shelf tag is still being printed.

faq.q: Which sellers should start from a packaging template?
faq.a: People who sell a packaged good and the person who buys ads for them. A roaster posting their own pouch, and a small agency handling five of those pouches, both start from this layout.

faq.q: Can I use one if I have never edited video?
faq.a: Yes. The three steps are enough, even if you have never edited a video. The front of the coffee pouch, photographed on a counter, is the start.

faq.q: Which kinds of shops can use these templates?
faq.a: The layout is not tied to one aisle, and this page starts from the coffee pouch you ship. A new roast keeps the same counter and the same front panel. Only the spoken line changes, so you are not rebuilding the shelf for the next bag.

faq.q: May the ad use photos and clips from my own shop?
faq.a: Yes. Put your own logo in the corner and a clip of the pouch if you filmed one. The product-page photo keeps the front panel identical to the bag you ship.

faq.q: Where can I place the finished pack ad?
faq.a: Place the file where the pouch already sells. TikTok takes the tall 9:16, the shop grid takes 1:1, a wide screen can take 16:9, and a Facebook placement can take 4:3 or 3:4.

faq.q: Do I pay to use the templates?
faq.a: Yes. Templates sit on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A photo is 24 credits. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the spend before it runs, and a failed job puts those credits back.

faq.q: Can I run these videos in paid ads and for clients?
faq.a: Yes. Run the clip as a paid ad, put it on the product page, or hand the file to a client who sells that coffee pouch.

faq.q: Why use a packaging video template?
faq.a: Your effort goes into what the pouch should say. A new roast keeps the shelf that is already in the layout, and only the spoken line changes.

reviews.h2: How Shops Preview a Pack on a Shelf
reviews.lead: Example shelf scenes, from a coffee pack to a pouch. This is not a check of print color or the small legal words.

items.t: A finished shelf frame from one pack photo
items.d: Example: a coffee shop uploads the bag and gets a square cafe scene to judge before a print order.

items.t: The mockup and a clip in one project
items.d: Example: a tea shop makes the tin picture and a short product clip together, in one project, without a second app.

items.t: Start from the bottle photo or the link
items.d: Example: a sauce shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the bottle, and the preview keeps that bottle's shape.

items.t: An AI actor and captions on the clip
items.d: Example: the pouch stays the shelf picture. On the video, the shop picks an AI actor, a generated person, then adds words on screen.

items.t: The same jar scene in another language
items.d: Example: the wood-shelf still stays as it is, and the spoken line on the clip is recorded again for a second market.

items.t: A voiceover and a track on the clip
items.d: Example: the carton preview is for slides you show a store buyer. On the video, the editor adds a spoken voice and a track from the music library.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a filmed spot
items.d: Example: a supplement shop uses an AI actor, a generated person, to hold the pack. Small ingredient text can blur, so the real label photo keeps the wording.

items.t: A digital twin for the next bag
items.d: Example: a pet-food shop uses a digital twin, the same generated person, so the next bag clip matches the first. No new light setup.

items.t: A script, then a second version
items.d: Example: a juice shop pastes the product link, takes a short script, and compares two bottle versions in the same scene.

items.t: Publish the clip, or start from the API
items.d: Example: after a look at the sample print, the shop posts the clip to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram). The API lets the product list start the next box.
